STRATA_QFUSE=1: a one-token window did not self-commit, but commit() skipped the commit graph as if it had (#3948)

Problem. #3948: with STRATA_QFUSE=1 the verified text changes and MTP acceptance drops, on CUDA. The QFUSE kernels are bit-exact
(gr_parity, gdn_parity, 10,500 random windows each on sm_86 and sm_120, after 91a4b8a67), yet the engine's greedy text still differed
from QFUSE off on every prompt tried. Model run, l620 (RTX PRO 5000, sm_120), Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S, MTP --spec 6, identity-gate
flags, 4 prompts of 4K and 12K tokens, 96 greedy tokens: QFUSE on differed from off on 4 of 4 (the off-vs-off control was identical).

Cause. A window of one token advances the GDN state and the indexer tail itself ("self-commit") so that commit() needs no commit
graph. Verifier::record_window decides this with
`T == 1 && !always_publish_ && !batch_rec_ && !g_qfuse() && one_token_self_commit()`: with STRATA_QFUSE the fused GDN output
kernel takes the q8_1 destination and the window does not self-commit. Verifier::commit() skipped the commit graph with
`last_t_ == 1 && !always_publish_ && one_token_self_commit()`, without the QFUSE term. So with QFUSE on, every accepted one-token
window left the recurrent state (and the indexer tail) one token behind. Windows of one token are the ordinary case when the drafter

Problem (KeyanHu-git, refs #2028, #2591): with STRATA_SPEC_PROB=1 the default

verifier still judged the draft against the unfiltered q and treated a failed gate as a

positive part of p - mu; a position with no attempted proposal is a plain sample from p.

verifier explicitly (Verifier::set_spec_proposal, sample_tokens_proposal). The explicit
call has no plain-p fallback: an invalid packet row is reported, not sampled around.

Conversation checkpoints: opt-in STRATA_CKPT_ASYNC (background device-to-host copy) and STRATA_CKPT_VRAM_SLOTS (#3779, #3712)

Problem: on a slow host link a turn checkpoint copies the whole GDN state to
the host on the request path (118 MB at 1.64 GB/s on a PCIe Gen2 x4 card, 72 ms;

- STRATA_CKPT_ASYNC=1: the GDN state is copied device to device into a VRAM stage
  (one buffer the size of the state, allocated at the first checkpoint save, plus
  a pinned host buffer of the same size; if either allocation fails the save falls
  back to the synchronous copy), and a background thread moves it in 4 MiB pieces
  into the checkpoint's host vector. Every reader joins first and only for the copy
  it needs (restore, snapshot save and restore, the parked copies, the serve loop at
  each request start, the SAVE/RESTORE session handler).
- STRATA_CKPT_VRAM_SLOTS=N (with ASYNC): the last N saved GDN states stay in VRAM,
  tag-checked, only allocated while 1.5 GB stays free; a restore of a checkpoint
  whose tag a slot holds copies device to device.

  timing of the save steps.

  snapshot, a tag field that stays 0 and a few clock reads; the copies are the

batch slots: MTP drafts in the pipelined groups, STRATA_PIPED_MTP=N opt-in with --batch-mtp (#4121, #3794)

Problem: a layer split with --batch pipelines the slots in groups, and the pipelined groups run no MTP drafts.
--batch-mtp with serial windows leaves all but one card waiting. A multi-stream deployment wants both.

What changed: STRATA_PIPED_MTP=N (with --batch-mtp) keeps the pipeline and drafts in it. A group's window carries
each of its slots' rows: the slot's token and up to N MTP proposals (at most --spec - 1; the first always, each
further one while the draft layer was at least --spec-min-p sure of the one before). The last stage judges each
slot's proposals on their own. The number of rows to keep is known only then, and by then the earlier stages run
other groups' windows, which reuse the scratch the commit replays from. So a small save graph copies those rows
right behind each window (Verifier::batch_launch_rows), and every stage queues the commit of the kept rows after
the verdict (Verifier::batch_commit_rows). The slot drafter catches up on its own rows and drafts the next
proposals as an asynchronous chain (MtpDrafter::chain_launch). Unset, nothing changes.

- The verifier window size is worked out where the verifiers are built, from the slots that fit and the final
  groups, not earlier from --batch as asked. Unset it is the old expression.
- STRATA_PIPED_MTP is decided again once the slots that fit are known. It says it is off, and why, when fewer than
  2 groups are left, when STRATA_BATCH_SELF_COMMIT is on, or when a group's window would hold more than
  kVerifyMaxT rows. The start line names groups and slots correctly.
- batch_groups::resolve keeps its old mtp_dropped rule; only mtp_piped is new, and it also applies with
  --batch-groups given (the PR's fix 1). The "--batch-groups 1" test case now expects "not dropped".
- --remote-expert-opt alone no longer blocks --batch-mtp on a layer split: the object it guards is only made with
  a helper expert cache (the PR's fix 2).

Prefill: opt-in STRATA_DEQUANT_SIDE=1 dequantizes the dense weights on a side stream into a double-buffered scratch (#3779, #3712)

Problem: Gemm::native dequantizes each dense weight to FP16 in front of its
GEMM on the compute stream, so the dequant never overlaps the kernels queued
ahead of it.

Change, opt-in (CUDA only, always off on HIP): with STRATA_DEQUANT_SIDE=1 the
prompt path takes a second GEMM scratch (64 MiB more of its region, counted in
bytes_needed and carried through relayout) and Gemm::set_dequant_side hands it
to the Gemm. native() then dequantizes the next weight on a non-blocking side
stream into the scratch the compute stream read last but one. Four events order
every write and read of each scratch (free -> dequant -> ready -> GEMM -> free),
so each product sees the same bytes as in the serial form. The row-sliced path
(a weight larger than the scratch) stays serial. Metal answers false and keeps
the serial form.

Differs from the PR as submitted: if the side stream, its events or the
setup fail, the PR failed the prompt-path init. Here one line is printed and the
dense weights are dequantized in front of their GEMMs as before. Unset, nothing
changes (gemm_dequant_side() is one cached flag; the scratch, stream and events
are not created).

eight Q4_K / Q5_K / Q6_K weights of the engine's shapes (one larger than the
scratch, so it takes the sliced path) run three rounds through Gemm::native
serially and with the side stream, with and without a spin kernel queued ahead of
each GEMM; every output must be identical bit for bit.

iq_kernels: GP100 4-bit gate/up expert slots, opt-in STRATA_EXPERT_NIBBLE=1 (#3455)

Problem: on a GP100 die the verify window's gate/up kernels for the IQ2_S,
IQ3_XXS and IQ3_S expert formats are not held by memory bandwidth but by each
block's serial chain (unpack the codebook indices, the emulated dp4a, the
16-lane reduction); the same kernel with every dot product removed still takes
about two thirds of its time.

Change: with STRATA_EXPERT_NIBBLE=1 the engine, after the expert cache is
filled and every expert is resident, transcodes the gate/up blocks of every
fully resident IQ2_S / IQ3_XXS / IQ3_S layer (n_embd 2560, n_ff 640) into slots
of 4-bit codes, 16 bytes per 32 weights, with the integer scales and fp16 d kept
as they are; the down rows stay GGUF. The decode gate/up reads those slots with
kernels that run the production integer chain and float tail in the production
order (R4S / R4P / R4SV / R4PX by format and group size); the prompt path's MMQ
gather rebuilds the GGUF blocks from a slot on the fly. At load every item is
round-tripped and every slot's rebuilt GGUF blocks are compared with the staged

layer-major prefill: a prompt that needs a run_impl feature the walk lacks takes the chunk-major path (#3976)

The layer-major walk is a copy of run_impl's attention half with the experts moved
out. It does not carry four things run_impl does, and when one of them is asked for

off for this prompt" line names the reason):

  stale and the drafter would read old rows;
- STRATA_KVA (approximate late layers): the walk would silently read exactly;
- a stop_at_chunk callback (the pipelined batch reader that yields at chunk
  boundaries): the walk reads every token, and stopped_at() must stay -1;
- a pending force_chunk (a --prefill-pipe plan): it is left set for run_impl.
The walk also resets stopped_at_ like run_impl does at the start of a run.

issued is a watermark, so a job nobody waits for could be passed while its thread was still writing
the pinned buffer the next job on that buffer was filling - a corrupt expert blob. A job now also
waits until the job kRing before it has marked itself ready. skip(j) lets a job the routing turned
out not to need be marked ready without reading it (the layer-major prefetch). The default walk
consumes every job in order, so neither changes it.

Port to 0.1.43.1: the stager now claims batched runs and sleeps in issued.wait, so the ready[i - kRing] wait
sits in the run's per-job wait loop after the issued wait, and a skipped job is left out of the run's gather

routed job it is about to wait for (store plus notify_all, which wakes sleeping threads); without it a routed

batch-groups: opt-in adaptive-tier rounds in the pipelined loop, STRATA_PIPE_ADAPT_EVERY (#4010)

With --batch-groups above 1 on a layer split the pipelined batch loop never starts a round of the adaptive VRAM tier (the
serial batch windows start one every --adapt-every windows). While the slots are busy the tier only moves when they go back
to the solo path, so a fresh engine keeps its start-up profile for minutes.

STRATA_PIPE_ADAPT_EVERY=N (opt-in; unset, 0 or not a number is off): after N group windows pump starts no new group on the
first stage, lets the groups in flight finish, then runs one round as batch_step does between serial windows, adapt() and
apply_pending(true), so nothing in flight reads a cache slot while experts swap and the new experts have landed before the
next launch. Not while a prompt is read beside the slots (in_prompt_read, its loan of cache slots), not with --adapt-async,
not while the last round's copies are in flight, not with the tier off. The rule is two pure functions in
include/strata/program/batch_groups.hpp (pipe_adapt_every, pipe_adapt_due) with 12 new cases in batch_groups_test. With the
switch set the engine says so once at start and the "strata batch (pipelined ...)" line adds the rounds, the experts
swapped in and the time spent. docs/BATCHING.md documents the switch with the author's table (2x RTX 5090, six streams,
309 to 410 rows/s over eight bursts after a fresh start, two engines per setting).

Reviewed: unset costs one counter increment per group window and one false check where a group starts, and prints no new
line. A due round cannot wait forever: no new group starts, the groups in flight finish, then the round runs. A prompt read
sets in_prompt_read before the reader thread starts (including STRATA_PIPED_CONCURRENT) and clears it after the reader
joined; the drain after the read runs the round if it is due.

experts the windows keep routing to take the RAM places of unused experts of their layer. Each move re-read the incoming
expert from the file and a layer moved one pair per window, although the incoming expert was usually read for the window

  and the pair then goes the old way. The Foresight hold/unhold around the copy is the one install_resident uses.
- generate.cpp: a layer pairs up to 4 of its most routed outside experts with up to 4 of its least routed ones in the copy
  (outgoing count below 0.5, incoming 2 or more), largest difference first. A pair whose incoming expert is staged moves by
  copy; `n` now caps only the pairs that need a file read. The log line counts the moves and how many came out of a stage
  buffer (ram_staged()).

- STRATA_PREFILL_COPY_EVENT_EVERY=N (2..64): the copied event is recorded every N-th entry, before the issuer waits and on

conversation copies: the private copy streams and events are handed back to a pool when a thread ends (#3350, #3470)

conversation_detail::private_stream() and order_after_queued() kept one non-blocking stream and one event per device in
thread_local storage and never destroyed them. The layer split's later stages run each prompt chunk on a fresh
std::async thread (STRATA_HANDOFF_PIPE off, the default), and a checkpoint part is saved on that thread, so every
periodic checkpoint of every long cold prompt left a stream and an event behind on each later card: a few MiB of VRAM
per long prompt that never came back (#3470: the later card's free VRAM drops 2-6 MiB per long cold prompt, no plateau),
until cudaStreamCreate failed with "out of memory" (#3350: "conversation snapshot running-state copy: out of memory",
engine exit) on a card that was already nearly full.

A thread now hands its handles to a process-wide pool when it ends and the next thread takes them, so the number of
streams and events is the number of threads copying at once. Same stream, same flags, same contract; only the lifetime
changed. copy_streams_created() / copy_events_created() count what the process made.

serve: a checkpoint whose copy runs out of memory is skipped, it no longer ends the engine (#3350)

A conversation checkpoint is an optimization, like parking, but the writer treated a failed copy as fatal: "conversation
snapshot running-state copy: out of memory" (cudaErrorMemoryAllocation from the snapshot copy: the private copy stream's
first creation or the driver's staging on a nearly full card, not host RAM) made the prefill fail and the engine exit,
21 times in 4 h for one reporter and 16 in 34 h for another, each exit a reload and the in-flight requests lost.

Now, after a failed save, checkpoint_failure_is_survivable() clears the non-sticky allocation error and synchronizes the
device: when that is clean the checkpoint is skipped with a line on stderr and the request goes on (a layer split's stage
part is left empty, which already means "no checkpoint at this length"; the message-boundary / turn / root checkpoints
after a prompt chunk do the same). A device that is unwell (a sticky error, a GPU that stopped answering) still ends the
request exactly as before. Same edits in sycl/src/program/generate.cpp.
